summary.text: 水 is a whole-character picture of flowing water: an undulating current with droplets beside it. Its common meaning is “water.”

formation.text: This is a pictograph: early forms depict a flowing current with side marks for droplets. The marks belong to one picture rather than forming separate characters. A Han-era explanation adds a cosmological account, which is distinct from this graphic construction.

components.text: The whole graph depicts flowing water. Early forms vary in their side marks; the central stroke represents the current and the marks represent droplets. These are parts of the picture, not separate character components.

history.text: Oracle forms vary in the number and placement of side marks. Bronze and Warring States forms are described as retaining the flowing-water picture. The selected oracle and bronze glyphs illustrate forms from those traditions, rather than proving a step-by-step sequence of changes.

A Han-era account glosses 水 as “level” and explains the graph through the cosmology of its time. This is a historical explanation of the character, distinct from the pictorial account of its formation.

uncertainties.text: Proposals for the spoken word’s earlier pronunciation and possible relationships to words in other languages differ. These concern the word’s history, not a sound component in the graph.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone examples; individual dates unresolved
senses.text: Reported Shang oracle-bone examples use 水 for water or flooding. The examples are not individually dated, so their relative order is unresolved.
The common current meaning is “water.” Other recorded glosses include liquid, lotion, and juice; their chronology is not established here.

A bronze inscription is reported to use 水 to write the different word 乞, “request.” In this proposed graph borrowing, the sign was reused because the words may have sounded alike or similarly; water did not acquire the meaning “request.” The historical sound match is unconfirmed.
One reported oracle-bone use is read as a verb involving either leveling ground with water or washing a temple. Its reading and its connection, if any, to the noun “water” remain unresolved.

developments.text: The graph is reported to have been reused for 乞, “request,” on the proposed basis that the words sounded alike or similarly. The old spoken name of the pictured water and a historical comparison of the two words’ pronunciations are not established.

limitations.text: The oracle examples are not individually dated here. Whether the disputed verbal use is related to the noun “water” is unresolved.
The proposed sound-based explanation for writing 乞 with 水 lacks a confirmed historical comparison of their pronunciations.
水準 is reported in compounds for a leveling instrument and, later, an abstract “standard” or “level.” These compound meanings are not separate senses of 水; the stages are undated here.

overview.text: 水 pictures flowing water: a central current with marks for droplets. Its common meaning is “water.”

components.text: Together, the central line and side marks picture a current and its droplets.
